exposure: Vitamin D supplementation (400 IU/day vs. 600 IU/day vs. none)
cohort: 60 pregnant women with vitamin D deficiency (<20 ng/mL)
finding: Vitamin D supplementation during pregnancy, at doses of 400 IU/day or 600 IU/day, did not significantly reduce the incidence of GDM or PIH, nor did it affect the mode or time of delivery.
mod_finding: While there was an insignificant trend towards an increased C-section rate in the group receiving 600 IU/day of vitamin D, no significant difference in mode of delivery was found between the vitamin D supplementation groups and the control group.
